title: Generalizations of nets and Latin squares
summary: We examine combinatorial structures that generalize $(k,n)$-nets, orthogonal arrays, and mutually orthogonal Latin squares. By a reticulation we mean a point set and two collections (types) of families of lines such that two lines of different types meet in exactly one point and each family of lines partitions the point set. The number of points incident with any line depends only upon the type of the line, and every point is incident with the same number of lines of a given type. Each choice of a single line family of each type leads to an arrangement of the points into a rectangular grid.…
